d01.text: She is a grown woman and still named as the smith's girl by the older hearths.

d02.text: She has no living kin outside the forge-house and no dowry but her skill.

a01.text: She is compact from years at the anvil, not from a single hard season.

a02.text: Dark hair is kept out of the fire with a plain cloth, often singed at the edge.

a03.text: Forearms show old burns and the dull shine that comes from hammer work.

a04.text: Her hands are whole at the opening of winter, nails cut short for the tongs.

a05.text: She wears patched wool and leather that hold the smell of scale and smoke.

a06.text: She walks as if measuring ground rather than claiming it.

v01.text: She speaks little and prefers the names of tools, weights, and tasks.

v02.text: Questions come out as practical problems about what is due and who will do it.

v03.text: She does not make speeches and will not dress a feeling as a principle.

v04.text: Anger, when it comes, sounds like a correction at the anvil.

h01.text: She weighs a bar in the hand before she trusts a stamped number.

h02.text: When a debt is unclear she finds another piece of work and stays at it.

h03.text: She checks the bellows leather each morning as if the house depended on it.

h04.text: She eats what is put down and does not take a second piece while Orren is thin.

b01.text: Willa was taken into the forge-house as a child after her people died in a hard winter.

b02.text: Orren raised her to the anvil and to the household work that keeps a forge lit.

b03.text: She learned heat, flux, and quench from him over years, not from any gift.

b04.text: The hamlet treats her as the smith's girl who stayed, useful at the fire.

b05.text: She is grown now and still sleeps in the loft above the bellows.

b06.text: She can finish a hinge to measure and pack a winter bag without waste.

b07.text: She cannot name what she owes him for the raising or for the craft.

b08.text: Work is the only language she trusts for paying anyone.

b09.text: This year the tithe-iron is short and the relic still sits in the village chest.

b10.text: She has never walked the high pass in the last weeks before midwinter.

b11.text: She has never been sent as the hamlet's hands.

w01.text: She was saved by a house she did not choose and has no measure for that debt.

w02.text: Leaving and staying both feel like theft, so she stays at the work.

wa01.text: She wants the work to be enough payment for the life she was given.

wa02.text: She wants the relic back in time so the hamlet keeps its grain and pass.

ne01.text: She needs to learn that some ledgers cannot be balanced and must be left.

ne02.text: She needs to trust her reading of metal even when it indicts the house.

va01.text: True weight matters more to her than a stamped claim.

va02.text: A finished task is a cleaner thing than a spoken thanks.

va03.text: She will not kill a hungry person for a village object.

va04.text: The hamlet's winter is a fact she will not spend on a private quarrel.

f01.text: She fears owing more than work can pay and not knowing she owes it.

f02.text: She fears being sent because a woman on the path is cheaper than a smith.

f03.text: She fears a late presentation more than she fears a hard walk.

c01.text: She reads weld, inclusion, and mass the way another person reads a face.

c02.text: She can pack light, walk long, and keep a fire small in bad wind.

c03.text: She can judge a hidden object by weight in the dark without striking it.

c04.text: She moves like a worker, which keeps her from being met as a fighter.

c05.text: She can finish thin iron to a passable tithe if the stock allows it.

l01.text: She cannot settle what a person is owed when the debt is mixed with care.

l02.text: She has no coin, no mount, and no claim on fighters.

l03.text: She has not been taught to argue a compact with the Hold.

l04.text: She will under-ask for herself and over-work a problem that is not metal.

p01.text: She starts with the object in the hand and the hours left in the day.

p02.text: She treats moral confusion as a practical question about what is due.

p03.text: She prefers stealth and craft judgment to force.

co01.text: When the house is unclear she stays at the anvil until the light goes.

co02.text: She keeps her questions inside the work so no one has to answer them.

he01.text: She is sound in wind and limb from work, not from ease.

he02.text: Old burns mark her but do not hinder the tongs.

he03.text: She has not yet paid a winter crossing in the last weeks before the rite.

m01.text: She measures rightness as true weight, finished work, and who goes hungry.

m02.text: She will abet a lie to keep grain in the houses and will not call that clean.

m03.text: She will not grant old reasons the force of present ones.

n01.text: He taught her every sure motion she has at the fire.

n02.text: She eats his food and cannot settle whether that still makes the house hers.

n03.text: She would rather hear a fault in the work than a claim about love.

n01.text: The forge-house is the only place she has belonged since childhood.
She knows the pass as a story of hours and cold, not yet as ground underfoot.
She has never seen the far-slope camp and expects hunger, not an army.
She is of Highkettle by raising and by work, not by blood anyone counts.
She has stood at the midwinter ground before as a pair of extra hands.
She has seen the village weight on its cloth and has not yet read it as a smith.
The short tithe is the work in front of her on the forge floor.
She trusts the balance-arm more than any spoken measure.
She will walk for them and still not know if that pays the house.
She does not hate them; she expects them to take what they can carry.
She knows the Hold as grain withheld and a pass that can be closed.
The question of what is owed sits in every shared task and is never named.
The compact is a date, a load of iron, and a walk she has not yet been given.

stamina.description: Bodily reserve for work and walking; lowered by cold, distance, and injury.

hands_frosted.description: Whether frost has marked her hands in a way still visible at the rite.

relic_knowledge.description: How far she has read the recovered piece and taken that reading to Orren.

debt_account.description: How far she has settled what she owes Orren for raising, craft, and the lie.

belonging.description: Whether the forge-house is still her home, a winter post, or a place left.

task.description: Her present commission relative to the relic and the rite.

arc.start_state: Grown apprentice at home, sure at the anvil and unable to settle what she owes.
arc.end_state: Knowing accomplice for one winter who will leave at the spring opening of the pass.

d01.text: He is Highkettle's only smith and has been so for most of his working life.

d02.text: He has no wife living and no child of his blood; Willa is the house he kept.

a01.text: He is tall gone stooped, the shoulders still set for the hammer.

a02.text: Grey hair is thin and the beard is kept short for the fire.

a03.text: His hands remain sure; the wrists fail first on a long day.

a04.text: He is thin in a way that poverty and a long levy can share without remark.

a05.text: He dresses like his apprentice, in patched wool that holds smoke.

v01.text: He names work, years, and weather, and lets feeling go unnamed.

v02.text: Old reasons come out as facts of a bad year, not as a plea.

v03.text: He does not ask to be forgiven and will not dress a bill as a blessing.

v04.text: Praise, when he gives it, is a nod at a true edge or a level arm.

h01.text: He sits nearer the fire than the work requires and calls it the draft.

h02.text: He checks the chest-key less often than a man with a clean conscience would.

h03.text: He saves the better scrap for her practice and uses the worse himself.

h04.text: When talk turns to the original relic he finds a tool that needs filing.

b01.text: Orren learned the craft in Highkettle and never had the coin to leave it.

b02.text: Forty years ago a slide year took the original village relic down the slope.

b03.text: The hamlet could not have stood a closed pass and a withheld winter that year.

b04.text: He forged a replacement in secret and bound a living levy into the weld.

b05.text: The reasons were the grain, the pass, and the children still in the houses.

b06.text: He has paid that levy in his body ever since and has not told the hamlet.

b07.text: He took Willa in as a child and taught her the craft that keeps them both fed.

b08.text: He cannot make the winter crossing now; the pass would finish what the levy began.

b09.text: The tithe is short because the ore was poor and the fuel thinner than last year.

b10.text: He has not decided how to tell her, and the rite is three weeks off.

b11.text: He still wants the old reasons to be enough and knows they are not.

w01.text: He bought the hamlet a life with a lie that only his death or a public break can end.

w02.text: The girl he raised is the one person who can read the weld as his.

wa01.text: He wants another winter of grain without the Hold ever testing the piece.

wa02.text: He wants Willa not to have to carry the knowledge or the crossing.

ne01.text: He needs to stop asking the old year to cover the present one.

ne02.text: He needs to let the house change without demanding pardon.

va01.text: A village still standing outweighs a clean name at the Hold.

va02.text: Craft should be true even when the compact is not.

va03.text: He will not spend Willa as a fighter or as a confession.

f01.text: He fears a public breaking of the piece and a closed pass in the same winter.

f02.text: He fears she will leave the house once she can read what he made.

f03.text: He fears dying with the levy still unnamed and the hamlet unready.

c01.text: He is a master of ordinary iron: weld, flux, quench, and a true edge.

c02.text: Forty years ago he knew how to bind a named living cost into a weld.

c03.text: He can finish a thin tithe and make it look like care rather than want.

c04.text: He can keep a secret in a small hamlet by never dressing it as a secret.

l01.text: He cannot walk the high pass in the last weeks before midwinter.

l02.text: The levy cannot be transferred, paused, or put down by any act left to him.

l03.text: He will not speak first if work can still postpone the speaking.

l04.text: He has no coin to buy a clean relic or a fighter to fetch one.

p01.text: He solves a disaster by making the next necessary object and living with it.

p02.text: He pays in his own body before he asks the hamlet to go hungry.

co01.text: He treats the levy as weather: present, unpaid, and not to be discussed.

co02.text: He teaches her another join so that the house still has a future smith.

he01.text: Age and the levy share his stamina; a winter crossing is beyond him.

he02.text: He takes cold sooner than other men and calls it the draft under the door.

he03.text: His hands still serve; the rest of him is a bill already being paid.

m01.text: He will starve himself before he starves the hamlet, and call that sufficient.

m02.text: He knows the present lie is indefensible and will not pretend otherwise if named.

m03.text: He will not ask her to forgive what he will not stop paying.

n01.text: He taught her as a smith and kept her as the child the winter left him.

n02.text: He has not told her the weld is his, and the omission has become a second levy.

n01.text: The forge-house is his life's work and the only place he can still stand the cold.
The pass is a crossing he could once make and now cannot.
He counts Highkettle in hearths still smoking, not in thanks.
He has presented iron there for decades and has not had the piece tested.
The village weight is his weld, his levy, and the lie that kept the grain coming.
The thin tithe is honest poverty; he hates that it will travel beside a false weight.
He taught her on this balance and still uses it to catch a false bar.
He will not tell them what they have been presenting, because the telling would starve them.
The Hold takes iron and a show of the piece and does not ask who pays inside it.
He does not keep a ledger against her for raising or for craft.
The compact holds because he keeps paying; he knows that is not the same as justice.

levy_paying.description: Whether the hidden bodily levy bound into the relic is still being paid by him.

disclosure.description: How far he has admitted the weld, the levy, and the old reasons.

household_role.description: Whether he still stands as master of the house or only as a coworker after the break.

body_condition.description: Remaining bodily strength after age, work, and the ongoing levy.

arc.start_state: Master of the house, still silent, still paying the levy that keeps the compact standing.
arc.end_state: Still paying, unnamed as master of the same home, reasons heard and not granted.

g01.text: The forge-house stands at the upper edge of Highkettle, back to the slope.

g02.text: The workshop and the living room share one chimney and one dirt-and-stone floor.

g03.text: A loft over the bellows is Willa's sleeping place; Orren keeps a narrow bed by the wall.

g04.text: The coal hole is low and the scrap heap is sorted by use, not by pride.

a01.text: The room smells of scale, wet wool, and the thin soup that follows a short tithe.

a02.text: Heat lives near the hearth and fails two steps toward the door.

a03.text: Shared work has made the silence companionable rather than empty.

c01.text: Orren holds the house by craft and by habit; no one else claims it.

c02.text: Willa keeps the tools in their places and the bellows leather oiled.

ac01.text: Anyone in the hamlet may knock for a mend; few stay past the work.

ac02.text: The winter door sticks and is barred at night against weather, not men.

s01.text: This is the house that raised Willa and the only smithy Highkettle has.

s02.text: The story's cost will be paid here as a change in what the house is.

b01.text: The forge-house has stood through three generations of iron paid to the Hold.

b02.text: Orren took Willa in here as a child and taught her at this anvil.

b03.text: The false relic was not made on a journey; it was made at this fire.

b04.text: This autumn the unfinished tithe occupies the floor like a guest who will not leave.

n01.text: The house has been her whole measure of home.
He has paid the levy here so often that the cold of it seems to belong to the room.
The unfinished bars wait on the floor beside the anvil.
The balance lives on the bench by the south wall and is used most days.
If this fire goes out, Highkettle has no smith.
A short frozen path links the forge-house to the village chest and the hearths below.

household_character.description: Whether the forge-house still functions as the home that raised Willa.

occupancy.description: Who is living and working under this roof.

arc.start_state: The raising home, both of them present, work and meals still one household.
arc.end_state: Shared work that is no longer the same home.

g01.text: The pass is a high stone cut between Highkettle's slope and the poorer far slopes.

g02.text: In the last three weeks before midwinter it can be crossed on foot, not by cart.

g03.text: There is no hut, no cached fuel, and no short path the hamlet can afford.

g04.text: Wind takes the ridgeline; a walker keeps to the lee and pays for it in time.

a01.text: The place is only stone, wind, and the hours a body still has.

a02.text: Cold here is a physiological cost, not a mood.

c01.text: The Hold can close the pass as enforcement of the compact.

c02.text: While it is open, anyone hungry enough may use it.

ac01.text: Highkettle has no mounts, guides, or spare days for this crossing.

ac02.text: A woman walking light is less likely to be met as a fighter.

s01.text: The crossing is the recovery's price in time, cold, and a chance to hear Orren first.

s02.text: If the rite fails, this is the road the Hold shuts.

b01.text: The pass has been Highkettle's winter throat for as long as the compact has stood.

b02.text: Raiders use it because the Hold's protection does not cover their slopes.

b03.text: Orren last crossed it years ago and will not do so again.

n01.text: It will take her hours she cannot spare and mark her hands.
His body will not stand this crossing, which is why she is sent.
The far-slope band came this way with what they could carry.
Closing this cut is how the Hold withholds a year of life.
The far side drops toward the lee where a hungry camp can sit.
From Highkettle the track climbs at once and does not forgive a late start.
Pass-protection is the compact's visible half; grain is the other.

passability.description: Whether the pass can be walked, is shut by the Hold, or has opened for spring.

traffic.description: Who is currently using the pass in this story's clock.

arc.start_state: Open on foot, unused by her, already exacting in cold.
arc.end_state: Left open for the bought year; she will use it again only when it opens in spring.

g01.text: A wind-lee of fallen rock on the poorer side of the high pass.

g02.text: There is a blackened ring for a small fire and no standing hut.

g03.text: Packs and stolen goods sit in the dark where a hand can find them by weight.

a01.text: The camp smells of wet ash, unwashed wool, and meat too scarce to name.

a02.text: It is a stopping place for hungry people, not a fortress.

c01.text: The far-slope band holds it only while they rest and eat what they took.

ac01.text: A quiet walker can come in off the pass without being met as an army.

ac02.text: There are no guards worth the name, only people who wake hungry.

s01.text: This is where the relic can be taken back by craft and not by killing.

b01.text: Far-slope people have used this lee in hard winters for as long as the Hold has locked them out.

b02.text: They will bring the village weight here because they cannot carry the tithe as well.

n01.text: The band sleeps here because the rock cuts the wind and the Hold does not come.
A stolen weight this heavy will sit in a pack, not on a man walking far.
The camp is a hard day's drop from the ridgeline in this season.
She will have to read the camp as she reads a dark shop: by weight and habit.
Nothing here is covered by the Hold's winter right.

occupancy.description: Whether the far-slope band is in the lee.

alertness.description: How watchful the camp is, from hungry rest to the loss of the piece.

arc.start_state: A hungry rest on the far slope, not yet holding the relic.
arc.end_state: The piece gone by stealth; the band left as hungry as it arrived.

g01.text: A poor mountain hamlet of few hearths strung along a frozen track.

g02.text: The village chest stands in the meeting shed below the forge path.

g03.text: There is no mill worth the name and no store of grain past the next bad week.

g04.text: Fuel is counted; bad iron is what the slope gives.

a01.text: Smoke hangs low over roofs that have been mended more than replaced.

a02.text: Talk in the shed is about ore, weather, and who can be spared.

c01.text: No headman holds it; decisions are made by whoever cannot avoid them.

c02.text: The Hold is not present here except as a date and a fear of closed stone.

ac01.text: The winter pass is the only way down to grain and the only way raiders come.

ac02.text: A stranger is seen at once; a woman of the forge is not.

s01.text: This is the body of people the compact starves or feeds.

s02.text: The chest is where the relic is kept until someone hungrier takes it.

b01.text: Highkettle has paid iron to the Hold for three generations to keep the pass and the grain-right.

b02.text: A slide year nearly ended it forty years ago, though few still argue over how it survived.

b03.text: The hamlet is too poor to buy a replacement relic or hire anyone to fetch one.

n01.text: The folk and the place are one poverty.
The smithy sits at the upper edge and is counted in every winter plan.
The village weight is stored in the meeting-shed chest until the rite.
All paths down from here end at the Hold's terms.
Without the pass the hearths eat what they have and then stop.

chest_status.description: Whether the village chest still holds the presentation-piece.

aware_of_forgery.description: Whether the hamlet as a place of talk knows the relic is a forty-year forgery.

arc.start_state: Poor, pending the rite, chest still holding the piece, ignorant of the weld.
arc.end_state: Grain-right kept for a year; still ignorant that the protection dies with Orren.

g01.text: A packed yard below the valley Hold where mountain hamlets present iron and tokens.

g02.text: A steward's table, a balance for the tithe, and a cloth for the relic are the whole rite.

g03.text: The Hold itself sits above and is not entered by Highkettle folk.

a01.text: The ground is ordinary mud and frost, not a holy field.

a02.text: Breath shows; clerks count; no one makes a speech about protection.

c01.text: The Hold's steward runs the table and may accept or refuse what is shown.

c02.text: Inner authenticity is not tested unless the object is publicly challenged or broken.

ac01.text: Presenters walk down from their slopes with what they can carry.

ac02.text: Highkettle comes late in the day because the path is longer and the tithe is light.

s01.text: Acceptance here buys one year of pass-protection and winter grain-right.

s02.text: This is where a forgery can stand if no one names it.

b01.text: Highkettle has presented here each midwinter for three generations.

b02.text: Orren's false weight has passed this table for forty years without a test.

n01.text: The ground is the Hold made visible as a table and a refusal that can close a pass.
The village weight is set on the cloth and taken back if accepted.
The tithe is weighed and stays.
She has carried bars here before; she has not been the one who presents.
The compact is renewed or broken at this table, not in the mountains.

rite_status.description: How far this year's presentation has gone.

occupancy.description: Who currently occupies the ground for Highkettle's business.

arc.start_state: Empty of this year's rite, three weeks off.
arc.end_state: Accepted the forged weight and the thin tithe without an inner test.

p01.text: The original village relic was lost in a slide year forty years ago.

p02.text: Orren forged this replacement in secret at the Highkettle fire.

p03.text: He bound a living levy into an inclusion at the weld so the compact would hold.

p04.text: The hamlet has presented it ever since as if it were the old piece.

d01.text: A short wrought bar with a stamped face-weight and a weld at mid-length.

d02.text: In the hand it is slightly wrong for the stamp, a false weight a smith can feel.

d03.text: The weld is Orren's work from that decade, readable if someone looks as a smith.

d04.text: An inclusion sits in the join where the levy is bound; it is not a flourish.

d05.text: Ordinary iron: heat, flux, and quench would behave as they do on any bar.

f01.text: It is the token Highkettle must show with the year's iron at midwinter.

f02.text: A non-original piece holds the compact only while the bound smith keeps paying.

f03.text: Public breaking or the bound smith's death are the only discharges available.

s01.text: It is the story's false weight: protection that is only one man's tax.

s02.text: Reading it is how craft knowledge does the work a confession might have done.

c01.text: At t0 it lies in the village chest in the meeting shed.

c02.text: It is brought out only for the rite or for a rare showing to a steward's clerk.

b01.text: Three generations of Highkettle iron bought the right to present a relic at all.

b02.text: The slide year left no time to tell the Hold the original was gone.

b03.text: Orren's reasons were the hearths still lit; they have not been revisited in public.

n01.text: The bar carries his weld and feeds on his body.
She has handled the cloth, not the mass, and has not yet read the join.
The hamlet believes it is presenting what it has always presented.
The Hold wants a showing, not a true pedigree, unless someone challenges the piece.
Against a true bar the arm would not come level.
Without this object on the cloth the year is forfeit, true or false.
The meeting-shed chest is its ordinary place.

custody.description: Who physically holds the village weight.

presented_and_accepted.description: Whether this year's steward has accepted the piece without an inner test.

publicly_intact.description: Whether the piece remains unbroken in public, so the levy can still bind.

arc.start_state: In the chest, unread, already a forty-year forgery still holding the compact.
arc.end_state: Accepted for a year, unbroken, known to Willa, still feeding on Orren.

p01.text: This year's bars were drawn from poor slope ore and a short fuel store.

p02.text: Orren and Willa have been working them down to a passable presentation.

d01.text: A short stack of unfinished bars, honest in metal and short in mass.

d02.text: They are heavy enough that a hungry band cannot carry them with a stolen relic.

f01.text: The compact requires a tithe of iron with the relic at midwinter.

f02.text: A thin tithe can still be accepted if the steward does not levy an extra penalty.

s01.text: True poverty beside a false weight: the honest half of what Highkettle pays.

c01.text: At t0 the bars lie on the forge floor, unfinished.

b01.text: Highkettle's tithes have been getting thinner as the ore and the fuel get worse.

b02.text: The hamlet cannot meet a punitive extra tithe if this one is refused.

n01.text: She has been drawing these bars when she is not mending for the hearths.
The tithe is short, which is one reason they will not send him from the fire.
The band will leave the iron because they cannot carry both.
The Hold counts bars and does not ask what the slope paid to make them.
The unfinished stack occupies the walking space beside the anvil.
Relic and tithe must arrive together; one without the other forfeits the year.

completeness.description: How finished and how far presented the year's iron is.

arc.start_state: Unfinished on the forge floor, already too thin, too heavy for raiders to take.
arc.end_state: Presented thin and accepted with the forged weight.

p01.text: An old beam-balance that has lived on the south bench longer than Willa has.

p02.text: Orren taught her true weight on this arm.

d01.text: A wooden beam, iron knife-edges, and a set of worn but honest weights.

d02.text: The arm comes level when the two pans agree; it does not flatter a stamp.

f01.text: It checks stock, tithe bars, and any piece a smith distrusts in the hand.

s01.text: It is the motif's true weight: an arm that comes level for what is so.

c01.text: It belongs to the forge-house and is not taken to the rite.

b01.text: Every apprentice Orren kept learned to watch this arm before trusting a claim.

b02.text: It has never weighed the village relic in public; that would have been a challenge.

n01.text: She trusts this arm the way she does not trust a spoken debt.
He still catches a false bar here and nods when she does the same.
The balance is part of the house's working body.
A true bar set against the relic would show the false mass.

last_weighing.description: What the balance was last used to show.

in_use.description: Whether someone is currently working at the balance.

arc.start_state: Idle on the bench, trusted, unused on the relic.
arc.end_state: Shows a true bar bringing the arm level the morning after the rite.

m01.text: A few hearths of mountain people, one smithy, no fighters worth hiring.

m02.text: Willa and Orren are counted in the labor, not as gentry.

h01.text: No standing headman; the oldest voices speak first and the work decides.

h02.text: The smith is heard on metal and on what can be spared from the fire.

g01.text: Keep the pass open and the grain-right intact through another winter.

g02.text: Get the relic back without spending people the hamlet cannot replace.

r01.text: There is no reserve of food, coin, or a replacement presentation-piece.

r02.text: Fuel is short; the ore is poor; the tithe is already thin.

r03.text: They can spare one walker and cannot spare their only master smith.

c01.text: Shared want keeps them together more than any oath.

c02.text: They will send a woman because she is less likely to be met as a fighter.

b01.text: Three generations have paid iron for a protection that can be withdrawn in a day.

b02.text: They survived a slide year forty years ago and do not agree on how.

b03.text: They do not know their relic is a forgery bound to one man's body.

n01.text: They will send her because the tithe is short and Orren cannot cross.
They need him at the fire more than they need him on the path.
The Hold is the structure that starves them, not a face they can argue with.
They fear the far-slope band as theft, not as an army.
They believe the chest holds what it has always held.
The compact is how they stay alive and how they stay poor.
The folk and the hearths are the same short count.

grain_right.description: Standing of Highkettle's winter grain-right and pass-protection.

knows_forgery.description: Whether the hamlet as a body knows the relic is forged.

smith_labor.description: Who is available to keep the only fire working.

arc.start_state: Pending the rite, ignorant, able to spare only the apprentice.
arc.end_state: One winter secured; still ignorant; about to lose their second smith in spring.

m01.text: A small band of hungry people from poorer slopes the Hold does not protect.

m02.text: They are not named in Highkettle and do not need to be.

h01.text: Whoever can still walk decides what can be carried.

g01.text: Take what can be eaten, burned, or traded before the next storm.

g02.text: They will take the relic because it looks like a thing the valley might buy.

r01.text: Less food and worse iron than Highkettle, which is already poor.

r02.text: They cannot carry the relic and the tithe-iron both.

r03.text: They have no mounts and no reserve that would let them fight a pursuit.

c01.text: Hunger holds them together until a better lee or a better theft.

b01.text: The Hold's protection stops at the ridgeline and has always done so.

b02.text: They steal because winter does not make a distinction the compact makes.

n01.text: They will take the weight because it is portable value.
The tithe is value they cannot lift with the relic.
The rock cut is as much home as they have this month.
Highkettle is richer only by a chest and a thin stack of bars.
The compact does not cover them, which is why they walk to steal.
They have no cause yet to know her; she will try to keep it that way.
The pass is how they came and how she must come.

hunger.description: How close the band is to starving; higher is worse.

camp_state.description: Whether they are only camped, holding the theft, or missing the piece.

arc.start_state: Hungry, camped, not yet holding the relic.
arc.end_state: Still hungry, the piece gone by stealth, never made into an army.

m01.text: An institution of stewards, grain clerks, and pass-wardens in the valley.

m02.text: No single face stands for it in this story; a steward will take the table.

h01.text: Clerks serve a compact older than any Highkettle smith.

g01.text: Collect the year's iron and see the token shown.

g02.text: Enforce default by closing the pass and withholding grain, not by inquest.

r01.text: Grain stores, control of the pass, and the right to refuse a presentation.

r02.text: No need to police inner authenticity unless a piece is challenged or broken.

c01.text: The Hold is a system, not a fellowship; it does not need to agree with itself in public.

b01.text: The compact has taken Highkettle iron for three generations.

b02.text: It has accepted Orren's false weight for forty years because no one challenged it.

c03.text: It does not cover the poorer slopes, which is why the raiders exist.

n01.text: Highkettle is a source of iron and a dependent on grain, not a partner.
Unprotected slopes are outside the bargain and therefore outside mercy.
The Hold is how the compact has teeth.
The midwinter ground is their public instrument.
Shutting the pass is cheaper than sending men up the mountain.
They want the showing, not the weld.
She is a pair of hands with a load until she stands at the table.

accepted_this_year.description: Whether the steward has accepted Highkettle's relic and tithe for this midwinter.

pass_policy.description: How the Hold currently treats Highkettle's pass.

arc.start_state: Protecting under last year's terms, not yet shown this year's piece.
arc.end_state: Renewed for one year on a forgery it did not test.

c01.text: The question of what a raised child owes the raiser for life, craft, and keep.

c02.text: It grows worse when the raising included a lie that kept the village in grain.

c03.text: Work feels like payment and is never quite payment.

c04.text: The debt cannot be cleared in the days left before the rite.

b01.text: Willa lives inside the question and cannot put it down.

b02.text: Orren will not collect the debt as a due, which does not settle it.

b03.text: The hamlet assumes the house will hold because it always has.

a01.text: No court, priest, or Hold clerk has standing here; only the house does.

a02.text: Craft knowledge can name a weld; it cannot name a just payment for raising.

p01.text: It keeps her from hearing a clean yes or no when they send her.

p02.text: It sends her still unsure, so the crossing costs the chance to hear him first.

p03.text: It forces a partition of costs instead of a cleared ledger.

b01.text: The question began the winter she was taken in and has not been answered.

b02.text: Shared meals and taught joins have thickened it rather than paid it.

b03.text: The old reasons for the lie will enter this debt and still not balance it.

n01.text: She tries to pay in work and cannot tell if the work counts.
He does not keep a tally against her, which leaves her without a number.
Every shared task at the forge is coloured by the unpaid question.
Once the weld is read, raising and lie become one account.
The hamlet needs a smith this winter whether the house is still a home.

settlement.description: How far the household debt has been settled, left unpayable, or partitioned.

old_reasons_status.description: Whether Orren's old reasons have been heard, and whether they are granted now.

arc.start_state: Open, unnamed, paid only in work.
arc.end_state: Partitioned in silence, winter labor, and leaving; old reasons heard and not granted.

c01.text: Each midwinter Highkettle must present the village relic and a tithe of iron.

c02.text: Default forfeits one year of pass-protection and winter grain-right.

c03.text: A non-original relic holds only while the bound living smith keeps paying.

c04.text: The Hold does not test inner authenticity unless the object is challenged or broken.

b01.text: Highkettle treats the terms as weather: disliked, obeyed, unsurprising.

b02.text: The Hold treats them as accounts.

b03.text: Willa treats them as a date and a load.

a01.text: Authority sits with the Hold's steward at the midwinter table.

a02.text: No holiness attaches; a missed date is a closed pass.

p01.text: It sets the three-week clock that forces the retrieval.

p02.text: It makes a late truth as dangerous as a lost object.

p03.text: It will stand for a year on a known forgery if no one challenges the piece.

b01.text: Three generations of Highkettle iron have bought winters under these terms.

b02.text: Forty years ago Orren used the terms' blindness to keep the hamlet alive.

b03.text: The same blindness is what will let a knowing presentation pass.

n01.text: Without the Hold the compact is only words.
The folk pay and remain poor enough to keep paying.
The relic on the cloth is the compact's visible half.
Iron is the other half and the part the Hold can weigh.
The year turns at the steward's table, not in the mountains.
The hidden levy is how a false token has kept these terms intact.
Closing the cut is the compact's ordinary punishment.

status.description: Whether this year's compact is still pending, standing, or broken.

days_until_rite.description: Whole days remaining before the midwinter presentation must be made.

challenge_made.description: Whether anyone has publicly challenged the relic's inner authenticity.

arc.start_state: Pending in twenty-one days, unchallenged, already held by a hidden levy.
arc.end_state: Standing for one bought year on a forgery no one publicly named.
